s: EUR amount: sum the line values in the transaction currency.
USD at the monthly average: multiply each line by its order month's rate (the agreed rule from Sprint 01).
USD at the March rate: multiply the EUR total by the March rate. The gap is pure translation.

code.title: Europe Q1 2026 in EUR and USD
src: WITH lines AS (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM order_lines),
SELECT ROUND(l.Qty * l.UnitPrice * (100 - l.DiscountPct) / 100.0, 2) AS GrossEUR,
JOIN orders AS o ON o.OrderID = l.OrderID
JOIN fx_rates AS fx ON fx.Month = SUBSTRING(CAST(o.OrderDate AS VARCHAR(10)), 1, 7) AND fx.Currency = o.Currency
WHERE o.Status = 'Completed' AND o.CustomerID <> 'C19999' AND o.Currency = 'EUR'
ROUND(SUM(GrossEUR) * (SELECT USDPerUnit FROM fx_rates WHERE Month = '2026-03' AND Currency = 'EUR'), 2) AS GrossUSDAtMarch

s: FY2026 week number = days since 28 Dec 2025 ÷ 7 + 1; quarter = (week − 1) ÷ 13 + 1; period = 3 × (quarter − 1) + (1, 2 or 3 depending on whether the week within the quarter is 1–4, 5–8 or 9–13).
Add the columns to the existing date table (Power Query or the date view); relationships stay on Date.
Sum gross sales by FiscalPeriod and compare with the calendar months: the boundaries move.

code.title: Fiscal periods 1–3 of FY2026 (SQLite JULIANDAY; SQL Server: DATEDIFF(day, '2025-12-28', OrderDate))
src: WITH lines AS (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM order_lines),
SELECT CAST((JULIANDAY(o.OrderDate) - JULIANDAY('2025-12-28')) / 7 AS INTEGER) + 1 AS FyWeek,
ROUND(ROUND(l.Qty * l.UnitPrice * (100 - l.DiscountPct) / 100.0, 2) * COALESCE(fx.USDPerUnit, 1), 2) AS GrossUSD
JOIN orders AS o ON o.OrderID = l.OrderID
LEFT JOIN fx_rates AS fx ON fx.Month = SUBSTRING(CAST(o.OrderDate AS VARCHAR(10)), 1, 7) AND fx.Currency = o.Currency
SELECT CASE WHEN FyWeek <= 4 THEN 1 WHEN FyWeek <= 8 THEN 2 ELSE 3 END AS FiscalPeriod,
FROM f GROUP BY CASE WHEN FyWeek <= 4 THEN 1 WHEN FyWeek <= 8 THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
